chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said concerning a man who ordered his slave to kill a man, and he killed him: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said: “Is the slave of a man anything but like his sword? The master is to be killed, and the slave is to be confined in prison.”

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: These two reports have been transmitted as we have cited them, but practice should rest upon the first report, because it accords with the apparent meaning of the Book of Allah and the many reports that we have mentioned earlier. For the Qur'an has stated that a life is for a life, and we know that it intended only the life that kills. The reports we cited regarding those who participated through watching, restraining, and killing also support this, because qiṣāṣ in them was imposed only upon the killer, and it was not imposed upon the one who restrained nor upon the one who watched. And we know that the one who restrains is graver in matter than the one who orders. So when the two reports conflict with the Qur'an and the reports, their force should be set aside, and practice should be according to what is besides them. However, the two reports can bear one interpretation: that they refer to one whose habit is to order his slaves to kill people, inciting them to that and compelling them toward it. In that case, it is permissible for the Imam to kill one whose state is such as this, because he is a corrupter in the land.

key_terms.السَّيِّدُ: the master; the slave-owner who issued the order
key_terms.السِّجْنِ: the prison; the place where the slave is confined
key_terms.النَّفْسَ بِالنَّفْسِ: a life for a life; the Qur'anic principle of retaliatory justice
key_terms.الْآمِرِ: the one who orders; the commander who instructs another to kill
key_terms.الْقِصَاصَ: legal retaliation; prescribed retributive punishment for unlawful killing
key_terms.عَبْدُهُ: his slave; the servant ordered to carry out the killing
key_terms.مُفْسِدٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ: a corrupter in the land; one whose conduct constitutes grave public فساد
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ: is to be killed; subject to execution

ai.seo_question: In Shia fiqh, is a master killed if he orders his slave to murder someone?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal ruling concerning a master who orders his slave to commit murder and presents a transmitted judgment from Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام. Shaykh al-Ṭūsī then explains that the operative ruling should follow the report more consistent with the Qur'an and other narrations, namely that qiṣāṣ applies to the actual killer, while these reports may be understood in the case of a habitual corrupter in the land.
